chunk.text:
## Accounting and recovery

Admission and the run's reservation journal commit in the same transaction,
before provider dispatch. The lock order is runtime ownership, project quota,
then accounting records. Administrator imports lock the project control row
and read committed journals without taking runtime leases. PostgreSQL row locks
and SQLite's immediate writer serialize competing processes.

Held cost is `committed_micros + in_flight_micros`. Uncertain cost is already
included in committed and is not counted twice. Outstanding attempts are
`in_flight_attempts + uncertain_attempts`: zero-priced requests occupy slots.
Known settlement releases only that attempt's slot. A lost response or killed
process retains its ceiling and slot; converting in-flight into uncertain does
not free capacity. The ledger does not silently refund or erase uncertain work.

A quota `Budget` refusal means a transaction was rolled back and no dispatch
was admitted. The runtime removes only the refused reservation and records the
budget stop without inventing uncertain fees. Other storage/commit failures
remain ambiguous and retain conservative uncertainty. Reservation registration
is serialized per run;

    "mount": "research",
    "mode": "active",
    "grant": {"tools":["knowledge_search"], "permissions":["knowledge:read"], "credentials":[]}
  }]
}
```

must enable knowledge access and set an explicit generation ceiling for output
repairs. Mount prefixes are 1–14 lowercase ASCII letters/digits/hyphens;
mounted role names cannot collide with host roles or other mounts.

chunk.text:
## Ownership, interruption and recovery

Claiming a job, increasing its attempt count and marking it Running is one SQL
transaction. Database time determines renewable lease validity. A candidate is
eligible only when both its queue owner and every associated runtime owner have
expired. A live owner is never stolen. Recovery claims are prioritized over new
pending jobs; healthy workers then take jobs in creation/ID order. This is not a
guarantee of fair CPU allocation among worker processes.

Run/workflow/session stores bind to the exact queue capability. Runtime writes
and pre-dispatch checks verify both fences, with another check before commit
after potentially expensive decoding/accounting. Generation reservations still
commit before each provider attempt. Removing a capability cannot authorize
dispatch through a plain SQL handle. Lease loss or an unverified monitor stops
new work; the former owner cannot overwrite the successor's checkpoint or budget.
External services are not transactional participants, so no exactly-once external
effect guarantee is added.

chunk.text:
## Accounting and recovery

Admission and the run's reservation journal commit in the same transaction,
before provider dispatch. The lock order is runtime ownership, project quota,
then accounting records. Administrator imports lock the project control row
and read committed journals without taking runtime leases. PostgreSQL row locks
and SQLite's immediate writer serialize competing processes.

Held cost is `committed_micros + in_flight_micros`. Uncertain cost is already
included in committed and is not counted twice. Outstanding attempts are
`in_flight_attempts + uncertain_attempts`: zero-priced requests occupy slots.
Known settlement releases only that attempt's slot. A lost response or killed
process retains its ceiling and slot; converting in-flight into uncertain does
not free capacity. The ledger does not silently refund or erase uncertain work.

A quota `Budget` refusal means a transaction was rolled back and no dispatch
was admitted. The runtime removes only the refused reservation and records the
budget stop without inventing uncertain fees. Other storage/commit failures
remain ambiguous and retain conservative uncertainty. Reservation registration
is serialized per run;

## Recovery, erasure and migration

Version-1 file snapshots live under `state_dir/memory/<scope-hash>.memory.json`.
Writes take per-scope OS locks, verify CAS/audit prefixes, flush a temporary file
and atomically replace the previous snapshot. Reads fail on corruption; they
do not silently reset state. Limits are 16 MiB, 4096 records, 16,384 forgotten
source bindings and 20,000 audit events. Admission also reserves 2 KiB, one
possible tombstone and one possible erasure event per retained record, so
administrative forgetting is not stranded by an admitted full snapshot.
A limit refuses the operation without
replacing the valid snapshot. Export/backup before planned migration; retain
the scope and revisions when implementing another `MemoryStore`.

Extraction request IDs bind a scope and the exact selected input to a durable
`memory-<hash>` child. Repeating a completed request with a fresh inspected
memory revision reuses its answer without another model request. If memory CAS
or capacity fails after generation, the completed extraction run stays in the
run store; inspect it and retry the **same request ID**, with the correct
revision/configuration. Do not silently mint a new paid r

## Trace and time semantics

`TraceSnapshot::run`, `workflow` and `session` build run or parent traces.
Workflow/node/durable-run and session/turn/durable-run relationships come from
persisted references and exact initial-input bindings. Closed session children
also match the recorded report fingerprint. Unreferenced, duplicate or mismatched
children fail; absent children are counted. Active durable children can be found
through their frozen node context before an outcome returns to the parent.
Reads of separate records are individually atomic, **not** a cross-record
transaction or a guarantee that a live parent and child were read simultaneously.

Stable SHA-256-derived IDs use a trusted host namespace and logical identities.
Revisions change the source revision key, not existing trace/span identities.
Changing the namespace changes IDs. The application defaults to a namespace
derived from its absolute state root; set an explicit namespace before moving
journals if continuity across deployment paths matters. These hashes provide
correlation and pseudonymization, not cryptographic storage authentication.

`lexical.stop_words` contains at most 256 lowercase normalized tokens, each at

changes this policy.

uses chunk body, title and the lexical metadata allowlist. Document IDs, source
paths and excluded internal metadata never become implicit searchable evidence.

chunk.text:
## Controls and limits

`lexical.stop_words` contains at most 256 lowercase normalized tokens, each at
most 64 bytes. It filters both query tokens and indexed fields when scoring.
The document and its citable body remain unchanged. Multi-token phrases and
non-normalized entries are rejected. Languages/domain vocabularies require
host review; filtering a meaningful token can reduce recall. Query aliases are
still expanded once by host policy before token filtering. Source text never
changes this policy.

`exact_identifiers` requires every query token that contains both ASCII letters
and digits and is at least eight bytes long to occur as an exact case-folded
token in each returned candidate. Token punctuation separates components. Pure
words, pure numbers and short names such as `Qwen3` are not constrained. Matching
uses chunk body, title and the lexical metadata allowlist. Document IDs, source
paths and excluded internal metadata never become implicit searchable evidence.
This intentionally narrow rule does not recognize every ticket/product-ID format.
chunk.title: docs/retrieval-relevance.md Controls and limits

chunk.text:
## Accounting and recovery

Admission and the run's reservation journal commit in the same transaction,
before provider dispatch. The lock order is runtime ownership, project quota,
then accounting records. Administrator imports lock the project control row
and read committed journals without taking runtime leases. PostgreSQL row locks
and SQLite's immediate writer serialize competing processes.

Held cost is `committed_micros + in_flight_micros`. Uncertain cost is already
included in committed and is not counted twice. Outstanding attempts are
`in_flight_attempts + uncertain_attempts`: zero-priced requests occupy slots.
Known settlement releases only that attempt's slot. A lost response or killed
process retains its ceiling and slot; converting in-flight into uncertain does
not free capacity. The ledger does not silently refund or erase uncertain work.

A quota `Budget` refusal means a transaction was rolled back and no dispatch
was admitted. The runtime removes only the refused reservation and records the
budget stop without inventing uncertain fees. Other storage/commit failures
remain ambiguous and retain conservative uncertainty. Reservation registration
is serialized per run;
chunk.title: docs/generation-quota.md Accounting and recovery

chunk.text:
## Trace and time semantics

`TraceSnapshot::run`, `workflow` and `session` build run or parent traces.
Workflow/node/durable-run and session/turn/durable-run relationships come from
persisted references and exact initial-input bindings. Closed session children
also match the recorded report fingerprint. Unreferenced, duplicate or mismatched
children fail; absent children are counted. Active durable children can be found
through their frozen node context before an outcome returns to the parent.
Reads of separate records are individually atomic, **not** a cross-record
transaction or a guarantee that a live parent and child were read simultaneously.

Stable SHA-256-derived IDs use a trusted host namespace and logical identities.
Revisions change the source revision key, not existing trace/span identities.
Changing the namespace changes IDs. The application defaults to a namespace
derived from its absolute state root; set an explicit namespace before moving
journals if continuity across deployment paths matters. These hashes provide
correlation and pseudonymization, not cryptographic storage authentication.

chunk.text:
## Ownership, interruption and recovery

Claiming a job, increasing its attempt count and marking it Running is one SQL
transaction. Database time determines renewable lease validity. A candidate is
eligible only when both its queue owner and every associated runtime owner have
expired. A live owner is never stolen. Recovery claims are prioritized over new
pending jobs; healthy workers then take jobs in creation/ID order. This is not a
guarantee of fair CPU allocation among worker processes.

Run/workflow/session stores bind to the exact queue capability. Runtime writes
and pre-dispatch checks verify both fences, with another check before commit
after potentially expensive decoding/accounting. Generation reservations still
commit before each provider attempt. Removing a capability cannot authorize
dispatch through a plain SQL handle. Lease loss or an unverified monitor stops
new work; the former owner cannot overwrite the successor's checkpoint or budget.
External services are not transactional participants, so no exactly-once external
effect guarantee is added.

remain ambiguous and retain conservative uncertainty. Reservation registration
is serialized per run;

chunk.text:
## Trace and time semantics

`TraceSnapshot::run`, `workflow` and `session` build run or parent traces.
Workflow/node/durable-run and session/turn/durable-run relationships come from
persisted references and exact initial-input bindings. Closed session children
also match the recorded report fingerprint. Unreferenced, duplicate or mismatched
children fail; absent children are counted. Active durable children can be found
through their frozen node context before an outcome returns to the parent.
Reads of separate records are individually atomic, **not** a cross-record
transaction or a guarantee that a live parent and child were read simultaneously.

Stable SHA-256-derived IDs use a trusted host namespace and logical identities.
Revisions change the source revision key, not existing trace/span identities.
Changing the namespace changes IDs. The application defaults to a namespace
derived from its absolute state root; set an explicit namespace before moving
journals if continuity across deployment paths matters. These hashes provide
correlation and pseudonymization, not cryptographic storage authentication.

## Accounting and recovery

Admission and the run's reservation journal commit in the same transaction,
before provider dispatch. The lock order is runtime ownership, project quota,
then accounting records. Administrator imports lock the project control row
and read committed journals without taking runtime leases. PostgreSQL row locks
and SQLite's immediate writer serialize competing processes.

Held cost is `committed_micros + in_flight_micros`. Uncertain cost is already
included in committed and is not counted twice. Outstanding attempts are
`in_flight_attempts + uncertain_attempts`: zero-priced requests occupy slots.
Known settlement releases only that attempt's slot. A lost response or killed
process retains its ceiling and slot; converting in-flight into uncertain does
not free capacity. The ledger does not silently refund or erase uncertain work.

A quota `Budget` refusal means a transaction was rolled back and no dispatch
was admitted. The runtime removes only the refused reservation and records the
budget stop without inventing uncertain fees. Other storage/commit failures
remain ambiguous and retain conservative uncertainty. Reservation registration
is serialized per run;

chunk.text:
## Trace and time semantics

`TraceSnapshot::run`, `workflow` and `session` build run or parent traces.
Workflow/node/durable-run and session/turn/durable-run relationships come from
persisted references and exact initial-input bindings. Closed session children
also match the recorded report fingerprint. Unreferenced, duplicate or mismatched
children fail; absent children are counted. Active durable children can be found
through their frozen node context before an outcome returns to the parent.
Reads of separate records are individually atomic, **not** a cross-record
transaction or a guarantee that a live parent and child were read simultaneously.

Stable SHA-256-derived IDs use a trusted host namespace and logical identities.
Revisions change the source revision key, not existing trace/span identities.
Changing the namespace changes IDs. The application defaults to a namespace
derived from its absolute state root; set an explicit namespace before moving
journals if continuity across deployment paths matters. These hashes provide
correlation and pseudonymization, not cryptographic storage authentication.

## Recovery, erasure and migration

Version-1 file snapshots live under `state_dir/memory/<scope-hash>.memory.json`.
Writes take per-scope OS locks, verify CAS/audit prefixes, flush a temporary file
and atomically replace the previous snapshot. Reads fail on corruption; they
do not silently reset state. Limits are 16 MiB, 4096 records, 16,384 forgotten
source bindings and 20,000 audit events. Admission also reserves 2 KiB, one
possible tombstone and one possible erasure event per retained record, so
administrative forgetting is not stranded by an admitted full snapshot.
A limit refuses the operation without
replacing the valid snapshot. Export/backup before planned migration; retain
the scope and revisions when implementing another `MemoryStore`.

Provider credentials/endpoints, model profiles and prices belong to the host

The file backend uses hashed run ids, a per-run OS lock, flushed temporary
files, atomic replacement and monotonic revision checks; saving a checkpoint
older than the stored revision fails with `Conflict` rather than reporting
success. The lock is held
throughout an invocation, including background file writes after an async
future is dropped. Other workers receive `Conflict`; they cannot execute the
same run concurrently. Persistent lock files are never unlinked. `inspect`

execution lock, so status can be viewed while a worker is active.

process briefly inherited a duplicate descriptor; active background writes

Only completed runs commit automatically. A failed terminal turn remains
bound until `abandon_turn` records an authenticated operator/application actor
and note. Uncertain/in-flight tools must first be reconciled through the
durable controller. Known observations stay in conversation history; calls
that were never dispatched receive explicit host error results. This includes
a call whose earlier attempt was reconciled with `RetrySafe` when the retry
itself never started; a call whose current attempt may have been dispatched
is never closed this way. An `Abort` reconciliation resolves the call with an
error result, after which the turn can be closed. A host note
records the failed outcome. This prevents an incomplete tool protocol from
leaking into the following model request, or a new question from silently
forgetting an uncertain write.

`commit_turn`/`abandon_turn` accept trusted controller state, not arbitrary
client-supplied JSON. The host application authenticates session access and
operator identity. A session is conversation state, not a cross-turn money
budget; each durable run keeps its own configured limits.

`OtlpHttpExporter::shutdown` refuses new work and waits up to its configured
timeout for admitted operations. On timeout it reports remaining work; callers
still own those futures, which retain their own request deadlines. There are no
exporter-created background workers to leak. Application shutdown uses this
method. A dropped/cancelled network future may have been accepted remotely;
repeat export is an explicit host decision, not an exactly-once guarantee.

# Project generation quotas

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer
uses the same project control lock, including Application/API/CLI, workflows,
sessions, memory extraction and direct `db.runs(scope)` calls. Creating another
pool or omitting a quota from a process configuration does not bypass a stored
policy. File journals do not gain distributed quotas.

This is generation accounting. Embedding has its separate ledger; generic tool
service charges remain separately unknown. A generation quota is not a durable
task queue, a rate limit or per-user billing. Separate
[queue/worker and bounded load evidence](durable-queue.md) covers those service
operations; broad native quality remains in P0.

or capacity fails after generation, the completed extraction run stays in the
run store; inspect it and retry the **same request ID**, with the correct

version of that slot from the memory snapshot. It retains only audit record
hashes and source-binding tombstones, preventing an old extraction of that same
source/slot from resurrecting the value, even if a later extractor proposes

This is memory-store erasure, not secure disk wiping or deletion of source
sessions, completed extraction runs, already frozen turn inputs, exports or
external backups. Those histories remain independently retained. New recalls
exclude forgotten records; old frozen inputs remain reproducible.

# Journal diagnostics and explicit OpenTelemetry export

`runtime::observability` projects **validated saved journals** into a correlated
trace. It performs no model, embedding or tool calls. There is no process-global
subscriber, automatic uploader, implicit `OTEL_*` environment discovery or
send-on-drop behavior. Network export requires the optional `telemetry` feature;
the application feature includes it, while default features remain empty.

## Trace and time semantics

`TraceSnapshot::run`, `workflow` and `session` build run or parent traces.
Workflow/node/durable-run and session/turn/durable-run relationships come from
persisted references and exact initial-input bindings. Closed session children
also match the recorded report fingerprint. Unreferenced, duplicate or mismatched
children fail; absent children are counted. Active durable children can be found
through their frozen node context before an outcome returns to the parent.
Reads of separate records are individually atomic, **not** a cross-record
transaction or a guarantee that a live parent and child were read simultaneously.

# Knowledge retrieval and source citations

Requires the preview's `runtime` feature. The complete offline pipeline is:

```sh
cargo run --locked --features runtime --example agent_research
```

It imports two Markdown files, chunks and indexes them, exposes a permitted
read-only search tool to a durable agent, writes a cited report, and verifies

| Interface | Built-in implementation | Replacement contract |

# Research sources and hybrid retrieval

`research` adds bounded webpage/search clients and an explicitly configured
Poppler PDF loader. `app` includes this feature but grants no web or PDF access
by default. Vector/hybrid retrieval is available with `runtime` alone.
These additions do not change the existing `AgentTask` API.

## Web sources and search

Merge the relevant section into the application's configuration:

```json

      "max_body_bytes": 2097152,
      "max_text_bytes": 131072,
      "max_redirects": 2,
      "timeout_ms": 15000
    },
    "search": {
      "endpoint": "https://api.search.brave.com/res/v1/web/search",
      "key_env": "BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY",
      "namespace": "my-search-tenant-v1",
      "access": {
        "allowed_origins": ["https://api.search.brave.com"],
        "allow_private": false,
        "max_body_bytes": 262144,
        "max_text_bytes": 131072,
        "max_redirects": 0,

System proxies, cookies and automatic redirects are disabled. Private network
access requires the separate explicit `allow_private: true` opt-in; use it

credentials are never forwarded through redirects.

Responses have total deadlines, hop limits and streamed byte limits, even
without Content-Length. Only UTF-8 HTML/plain text/Markdown is accepted.
HTML extraction excludes scripts, styles, templates, SVGs and frames; it never
executes JavaScript or fetches subresources. `timeout_ms` covers the whole
fetch including extraction. At most four HTML workers run concurrently.
The HTML5 tokenizer handles quoted attributes, raw text and foreign content;
a guarded tree builder checks the deadline per token and bounds its live
open-element/formatting references to 512. Input is fed in bounded UTF-8 chunks
with deadline checks, so tokenization also stops without requiring a closing
tag. An expired request cannot leave an unrestricted full-document parse
running. Text extraction then traverses the tree once, skipping excluded
subtrees. Script-rendered pages, login flows,

# Project generation quotas

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer
uses the same project control lock, including Application/API/CLI, workflows,
sessions, memory extraction and direct `db.runs(scope)` calls. Creating another

task queue, a rate limit or per-user billing. Separate

## Accounting and recovery

Admission and the run's reservation journal commit in the same transaction,
before provider dispatch. The lock order is runtime ownership, project quota,
then accounting records. Administrator imports lock the project control row
and read committed journals without taking runtime leases. PostgreSQL row locks
and SQLite's immediate writer serialize competing processes.

Held cost is `committed_micros + in_flight_micros`. Uncertain cost is already
included in committed and is not counted twice. Outstanding attempts are
`in_flight_attempts + uncertain_attempts`: zero-priced requests occupy slots.
Known settlement releases only that attempt's slot. A lost response or killed
process retains its ceiling and slot; converting in-flight into uncertain does
not free capacity. The ledger does not silently refund or erase uncertain work.

A quota `Budget` refusal means a transaction was rolled back and no dispatch
was admitted. The runtime removes only the refused reservation and records the
budget stop without inventing uncertain fees. Other storage/commit failures
remain ambiguous and retain conservative uncertainty. Reservation registration

# Explicit Linux-container Python execution

The optional `sandbox` feature exposes `CodeSandbox`, `DockerSandbox` and
`SandboxTool`. `app` includes the feature but registers no execution tool until
the host supplies `sandbox` configuration. Even then, only workflow roles that
list the tool receive it, unless `sandbox_top_level` is set. A missing Docker engine, missing
image or failed container never falls back to host Python or a host shell.

## Isolation contract

Only code is model-controlled. The host fixes the Docker CLI, local engine
socket/pipe, immutable audited image, platform, CPU/memory/output/time limits.
The model cannot select an executable, image, mount, network, package, device,
environment variable or Docker option. Code is sent through stdin, not shell
command text or host argv interpolation. The host passes only the code's byte
length and SHA-256 as supervisor arguments (`--code-bytes`, `--code-sha256`).
End of stdin alone does not prove the write completed, because an interrupted
controller also closes stdin. The supervisor therefore refuses to run anything
unless it received exactly the declared bytes with the declared digest. On
refusal it returns exit code 12

The supplied image's Python supervisor runs as **container PID 1 and uid 0**,
with only SETUID/SETGID capabilities. Its untrusted child runs as uid/gid 65534,
without those privileges, and cannot signal the root monitor. The monitor owns
the wall deadline and combined stdout/stderr byte ceiling. It returns a bounded
JSON packet and exits container PID 1 on timeout, excessive output or completion,
causing the container runtime to kill remaining namespace processes even if
they detached from the original process group. This deadline survives loss of
the host controller; it does not depend solely on killing `docker run`.
Ingress is also nonblocking and deadline-bound if the controller dies before
stdin EOF. Final response writing has a 500 ms grace before unconditional PID 1
exit, so an abandoned/nonreading output connection cannot keep code running.

## Session size limit

Every turn's run starts from the full session history, and each checkpoint
rewrites the whole run state, so a long session eventually approaches the
store's byte limit (64 MiB by default for both `FileSessionStore` and
`FileRunStore`; keep the session limit at least as large as the run limit).
To avoid a run that completes but can no longer be saved or committed, work is
refused **before** it starts:

- `begin_turn` (and so `run_turn`) rejects a new turn with
  `RuntimeError::StorageLimit` once the serialized session exceeds half of the
  session store's limit. Nothing is bound or dispatched.
- The new input and the metadata needed to close its turn must also fit;
  oversized input is rejected before the active binding is written.

## Session size limit

Every turn's run starts from the full session history, and each checkpoint
rewrites the whole run state, so a long session eventually approaches the
store's byte limit (64 MiB by default for both `FileSessionStore` and
`FileRunStore`; keep the session limit at least as large as the run limit).
To avoid a run that completes but can no longer be saved or committed, work is
refused **before** it starts:

- `begin_turn` (and so `run_turn`) rejects a new turn with
  `RuntimeError::StorageLimit` once the serialized session exceeds half of the
  session store's limit. Nothing is bound or dispatched.
- The new input and the metadata needed to close its turn must also fit;
  oversized input is rejected before the active binding is written.
- Managed execution subtracts the complete session commit metadata from its
  byte allowance. A durable run reserves the largest declared model/tool
  response, duplicated tool state, context projection and a terminal-record
  margin before dispatch. Insufficient space produces `Storage
chunk.title: Sessions and bounded model context

chunk.text:
ut must never be treated as permission to start another job.

Only completed runs commit automatically. A failed terminal turn remains
bound until `abandon_turn` records an authenticated operator/application actor
and note. Uncertain/in-flight tools must first be reconciled through the
durable controller. Known observations stay in conversation history; calls
that were never dispatched receive explicit host error results. This includes
a call whose earlier attempt was reconciled with `RetrySafe` when the retry
itself never started; a call whose current attempt may have been dispatched
is never closed this way. An `Abort` reconciliation resolves the call with an
error result, after which the turn can be closed. A host note
records the failed outcome. This prevents an incomplete tool protocol from
leaking into the following model request, or a new question from silently
forgetting an uncertain write.

`commit_turn`/`abandon_turn` accept trusted controller state, not arbitrary
client-supplied JSON. The host application authenticates session access and
operator identity. A session is conversation state, not a cross-turn money
budget; each durable run keeps its own configured limits.

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer
uses the same project control lock, including Application/API/CLI, workflows,

Admission and the run's reservation journal commit in the same transaction,
before provider dispatch. The lock order is runtime ownership, project quota,
then accounting records. Administrator imports lock the project control row
and read committed journals without taking runtime leases. PostgreSQL row locks
and SQLite's immediate writer serialize competing processes.

process retains its ceiling and slot; converting in-flight into uncertain does
not free capacity. The ledger does not silently refund or erase uncertain work.

was admitted. The runtime removes only the refused reservation and records the
budget stop without inventing uncertain fees. Other storage/commit failures

# Project generation quotas

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer
uses the same project control lock, including Application/API/CLI, workflows,

Admission and the run's reservation journal commit in the same transaction,
before provider dispatch. The lock order is runtime ownership, project quota,
then accounting records. Administrator imports lock the project control row
and read committed journals without taking runtime leases. PostgreSQL row locks
and SQLite's immediate writer serialize competing processes.

not free capacity. The ledger does not silently refund or erase uncertain work.

## Accounting and recovery

Admission and the run's reservation journal commit in the same transaction,
before provider dispatch. The lock order is runtime ownership, project quota,
then accounting records. Administrator imports lock the project control row
and read committed journals without taking runtime leases. PostgreSQL row locks
and SQLite's immediate writer serialize competing processes.

Held cost is `committed_micros + in_flight_micros`. Uncertain cost is already
included in committed and is not counted twice. Outstanding attempts are
`in_flight_attempts + uncertain_attempts`: zero-priced requests occupy slots.
Known settlement releases only that attempt's slot. A lost response or killed
process retains its ceiling and slot; converting in-flight into uncertain does
not free capacity. The ledger does not silently refund or erase uncertain work.

A quota `Budget` refusal means a transaction was rolled back and no dispatch
was admitted. The runtime removes only the refused reservation and records the
budget stop without inventing uncertain fees. Other storage/commit failures
remain ambiguous and retain conservative uncertainty. Reservation registration
is seriali

automatic calendar reset, historical currency conversion, pruning/refund API or
renewable rate window in this increment.

## Schema-v2 migration

Schema v2 introduced the generation-quota barrier. The current
`SqlDatabase::migrate` / `taskloom database-migrate` creates schema v3 or upgrades
v1/v2 in one transaction, including queue indexes/ownership. Stop all old hosts and workers first. Upgrade
refuses while any database-clock lease is live; PostgreSQL also locks the lease
table during the version barrier. Dataset UUID and existing version-1 JSON
envelopes/runtime checkpoints are preserved. Unknown versions and downgrades are
refused. Back up the complete database before upgrading and restore the complete
backup with its matching binary if rollback is required.

# Data-only skills, templates and connectors

The `runtime` SDK and optional `app` host support installable, content-pinned
skill packages. They contain UTF-8 guidance, typed role/output contracts,
workflow templates and connector configuration examples. Installation stores
inert JSON objects: it does not execute scripts, register a tool, start a
service, read a declared credential or grant a permission.

## Package format and authoring

Examples live in `examples/skills/`:

| Package | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `evidence-base` | Reusable evidence and permission guidance dependency |
| `research-brief` | Local corpus research role and cited source-summary template |
| `connector-notes` | Repository metadata, note-status and approved note-append templates |

Each directory has a root `skill.json`. Format 1 declares name, exact version,
description, SHA-256 for every asset, exact dependency `{name,version,digest}`
pins, tool effects/permissions, required credential **names**, roles, templates
and optional connector-example metadata. Names use lowercase ASCII letters,
digits and hyphens; versions are exact canonical `major.minor.patch` integer
triples. Ranges, prereleases, network URLs, i

chunk.text:
text, title, source and original byte range. A denied tool is not exposed or
executed. Its read-only effect permits ordinary durable recovery; importing or
deleting documents is a separate explicit host action.

Retrieved text can contain malicious instructions. The supplied examples treat
it as untrusted evidence in the system prompt, and tool policy independently
controls capabilities. Prompt wording does not provide a security sandbox.
External retriever service charges are outside the agent's model-spend budget.

## Citation verification and its limits

Ask the model for `CitedReport { text, citations: [{ chunk_id, quote }] }`.
The text uses `[[full_chunk_id]]` references. Validate it using the actual
`SearchResult::verify` from the run's tool output, not a new search of a possibly
updated corpus. Verification rejects unknown/unretrieved sources, duplicate
citations, chunks whose text no longer matches their own ID, absent or invented
quotes, quotes below the minimum size, absent/unclosed markers and references
without corresponding citations.

A quote must be an exact substring of the cited chunk and long enough to be
meaningful: by default at least 12 non-whitespace characte
chunk.title: Knowledge retrieval and source citations

chunk.text:
esearch`
feature adds bounded HTML/web and trusted Poppler PDF extraction. Office formats
still require a host loader. Sources are data; their references are not
automatically followed. This library does not sandbox custom loaders.

`ingest` validates document and plugin chunks before changing storage. Importing
the same document ID atomically replaces its prior chunks; it does not append
stale versions. A chunk ID hashes its document ID, title, source, exact text and
byte range. Updated provenance/content produces a new identity. Remove uses the
same optional expected-revision contract; stale CAS operations fail without
mutating the existing corpus.

File storage captures an absolute root, serializes writers with an OS lock,

# Research sources and hybrid retrieval

`research` adds bounded webpage/search clients and an explicitly configured
Poppler PDF loader. `app` includes this feature but grants no web or PDF access
by default. Vector/hybrid retrieval is available with `runtime` alone.
These additions do not change the existing `AgentTask` API.

System proxies, cookies and automatic redirects are disabled. Private network

Responses have total deadlines, hop limits and streamed byte limits, even
without Content-Length. Only UTF-8 HTML/plain text/Markdown is accepted.
HTML extraction excludes scripts, styles, templates, SVGs and frames; it never

with deadline checks, so tokenization also stops without requiring a closing
tag. An expired request cannot leave an unrestricted full-document parse
running. Text extraction then traverses the tree once, skipping excluded
subtrees. Script-rendered pages, login flows,

# Project generation quotas

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer
uses the same project control lock, including Application/API/CLI, workflows,
sessions, memory extraction and direct `db.runs(scope)` calls. Creating another
pool or omitting a quota from a process configuration does not bypass a stored
policy. File journals do not gain distributed quotas.

This is generation accounting. Embedding has its separate ledger; generic tool
service charges remain separately unknown. A generation quota is not a durable
task queue, a rate limit or per-user billing. Separate
[queue/worker and bounded load evidence](durable-queue.md) covers those service
operations; broad native quality remains in P0.

## Accounting and recovery

Admission and the run's reservation journal commit in the same transaction,
before provider dispatch. The lock order is runtime ownership, project quota,
then accounting records. Administrator imports lock the project control row
and read committed journals without taking runtime leases. PostgreSQL row locks
and SQLite's immediate writer serialize competing processes.

Held cost is `committed_micros + in_flight_micros`. Uncertain cost is already
included in committed and is not counted twice. Outstanding attempts are
`in_flight_attempts + uncertain_attempts`: zero-priced requests occupy slots.
Known settlement releases only that attempt's slot. A lost response or killed
process retains its ceiling and slot; converting in-flight into uncertain does
not free capacity. The ledger does not silently refund or erase uncertain work.

A quota `Budget` refusal means a transaction was rolled back and no dispatch
was admitted. The runtime removes only the refused reservation and records the
budget stop without inventing uncertain fees. Other storage/commit failures
remain ambiguous and retain conservative uncertainty. Reservation registration

The optional `sandbox` feature exposes `CodeSandbox`, `DockerSandbox` and
`SandboxTool`. `app` includes the feature but registers no execution tool until
the host supplies `sandbox` configuration. Even then, only workflow roles that
list the tool receive it, unless `sandbox_top_level` is set. A missing Docker engine, missing
image or failed container never falls back to host Python or a host shell.

## Isolation contract

Only code is model-controlled. The host fixes the Docker CLI, local engine
socket/pipe, immutable audited image, platform, CPU/memory/output/time limits.
The model cannot select an executable, image, mount, network, package, device,
environment variable or Docker option. Code is sent through stdin, not shell
command text or host argv interpolation. The host passes only the code's byte
length and SHA-256 as supervisor arguments (`--code-bytes`, `--code-sha256`).
End of stdin alone does not prove the write completed, because an interrupted
controller also closes stdin. The supervisor therefore refuses to run anything
unless it received exactly the declared bytes with the declared digest. On
refusal it returns exit code 12

base image to an immutable digest, review `sandbox/python/supervisor.py`, build
the supplied Dockerfile, then pin the resulting image ID/digest. For Linux:

```sh
DOCKER=/usr/bin/docker
ENGINE=unix:///var/run/docker.sock
$DOCKER --host "$ENGINE" pull python:3.12-slim
BASE_IMAGE=$($DOCKER --host "$ENGINE" image inspect --format '{{index .RepoDigests 0}}' python:3.12-slim)
$DOCKER --host "$ENGINE" build --platform linux/amd64 --build-arg BASE_IMAGE="$BASE_IMAGE" -t taskloom-sandbox:local sandbox/python
IMAGE=$($DOCKER --host "$ENGINE" image inspect --format '{{.Id}}' taskloom-sandbox:local)
```

The supervisor contract changed when the code-length/SHA-256 check was added:
`supervisor.py` now requires `--code-bytes` and `--code-sha256`. Rebuild
the image, which gives it a new digest, and update the pinned `image`. An
image built from an older supervisor rejects the new arguments, so every call
fails with a Docker execution error instead of running unchecked code. The 2026-11-27
acceptance record below names the earlier image and supervisor build-context

The supplied image's Python supervisor runs as **container PID 1 and uid 0**,
with only SETUID/SETGID capabilities. Its untrusted child runs as uid/gid 65534,
without those privileges, and cannot signal the root monitor. The monitor owns
the wall deadline and combined stdout/stderr byte ceiling. It returns a bounded
JSON packet and exits container PID 1 on timeout, excessive output or completion,
causing the container runtime to kill remaining namespace processes even if
they detached from the original process group. This deadline survives loss of
the host controller; it does not depend solely on killing `docker run`.
Ingress is also nonblocking and deadline-bound if the controller dies before
stdin EOF. Final response writing has a 500 ms grace before unconditional PID 1
exit, so an abandoned/nonreading output connection cannot keep code running.

Queue histories are bounded to 2048 events/1024 claims per job. New work is
refused before these limits exhaust outcome-recording capacity; oversized or
corrupt histories are never truncated or silently reset. Host-only malformed task
payloads become Failed without model dispatch. Generic SDK jobs outside the

# Durable SQL queues and workers

The `app,database` features provide explicit SQLite/PostgreSQL project queues
and independent worker processes. Submission persists immutable task input and
host contracts before execution. Workers reuse the existing durable run,
workflow, PEER and session controllers; a second job log never decides that an
unknown external write is safe to repeat.

Default features remain empty. File-based/local execution and `AgentTask` remain
compatible, with Rust 1.86. Queues are explicitly configured by a trusted local
administrator. The multi-user JSON service uses the same SQL project and live
role/token checks. The existing browser UI is the local operator UI; queue
submission/control currently uses the queue API or CLI. Legacy `job.active`
fields describe process-local workers. **Use queue job state and its runtime
bindings for distributed activity**, including a worker running on another host.

## Setup and migration

1. Stop old API hosts and workers. Back up the complete database and separately
   protect host configs, credentials, model weights and external tool data.
2. Build/install with `app,database` and run `taskloom database-migrate` against

Failed/timed-out/unusable results from a tool with effects also require
reconciliation. Use `reconcile` with a matching call id and an operator record:

- `RecordResult`: after inspecting the external system, supply the known
  result. It completes that exact call without invoking the tool again.
- `RetrySafe`: only read-only/idempotent tools are eligible. The same run/call
  ids are reused for tool-side deduplication. It requires fresh approval where

  finishes before the retry is dispatched (for example, the fresh approval
  is rejected, a limit is reached or the run is cancelled), the call stays
  pending and a session turn can still be closed: the earlier attempt was
  already reconciled, and the host result records that its outcome is unknown.
- `Abort`: terminate the run without continuing the uncertain operation. The
  call is resolved with an explicit error result recording the actor, note
  and an unknown external outcome, so the run can be closed and the abort
  cannot be repeated.

a non-idempotent tool leaves the original approved call uncertain. A replacement
classifies the saved intent and waits for observed operator reconciliation; it

silently reactivate them. In-flight tools remain marked uncertain for audit.
Recording a known result afterward does not reactivate a cancelled run.
`DurableAgent::cancel` records the operator's actor and note for an unowned
run. To attribute a cancellation of a live worker the same way, give it a
`CancelReason` with `with_cancel_reason`, call `record(actor, note)`, then
fire the cancellation token; the terminal checkpoint's detail reads
`cancelled by <actor>: <note>`. The application server does this for runs,
session turns and workflow children.

Step/tool limits and model spending accumulate across invocations. The elapsed
limit counts cumulative active execution, rounded up to milliseconds; known
pause/approval downtime is excluded. When a process dies during an operation,
the interval since its persisted wall-clock start is charged conservatively,
including unknown downtime. A backwards wall clock at recovery is rejected.

## Approval of exact input

Persistent runs require approval for idempotent/non-idempotent effects by
default. `ApprovalPolicy` can additionally require reads/named tools, or let
the host explicitly preauthorize a different policy at creation.

Only completed runs commit automatically. A failed terminal turn remains
bound until `abandon_turn` records an authenticated operator/application actor
and note. Uncertain/in-flight tools must first be reconciled through the
durable controller. Known observations stay in conversation history; calls
that were never dispatched receive explicit host error results. This includes
a call whose earlier attempt was reconciled with `RetrySafe` when the retry
itself never started; a call whose current attempt may have been dispatched
is never closed this way. An `Abort` reconciliation resolves the call with an
error result, after which the turn can be closed. A host note
records the failed outcome. This prevents an incomplete tool protocol from
leaking into the following model request, or a new question from silently
forgetting an uncertain write.

`commit_turn`/`abandon_turn` accept trusted controller state, not arbitrary
client-supplied JSON. The host application authenticates session access and
operator identity. A session is conversation state, not a cross-turn money
budget; each durable run keeps its own configured limits.

## Session size limit

Every turn's run starts from the full session history, and each checkpoint
rewrites the whole run state, so a long session eventually approaches the
store's byte limit (64 MiB by default for both `FileSessionStore` and
`FileRunStore`; keep the session limit at least as large as the run limit).
To avoid a run that completes but can no longer be saved or committed, work is
refused **before** it starts:

- `begin_turn` (and so `run_turn`) rejects a new turn with
  `RuntimeError::StorageLimit` once the serialized session exceeds half of the
  session store's limit. Nothing is bound or dispatched.
- The new input and the metadata needed to close its turn must also fit;
  oversized input is rejected before the active binding is written.
- Managed execution subtracts the complete session commit metadata from its
  byte allowance. A durable run reserves the largest declared model/tool
  response, duplicated tool state, context projection and a terminal-record
  margin before dispatch. Insufficient space produces `Storage

error result, after which the turn can be closed. A host note
records the failed outcome. This prevents an incomplete tool protocol from
leaking into the following model request, or a new question from silently
forgetting an uncertain write.

client-supplied JSON. The host application authenticates session access and

The event log is not capped: load-time validation checks every node's
dispatch counter against its `NodeStarted` events, so dropping old events
would weaken corruption detection. Its growth is bounded instead. A resume
that records nothing and ends in the status it started from (for example a
paused workflow resumed with the pause signal still set) leaves the log
unchanged and emits nothing to the event sink. Every other invocation either
dispatches (bounded by `max_dispatches`), changes status or resolves an
uncertain node, so the log grows with dispatches and node count, plus one
`Resumed` event per controller that died before recording anything else.

chunk.text:
leading system instructions, the current user
question and the latest complete block. An assistant tool request plus all
its results is an indivisible block, including batches with multiple calls.
Recent blocks are retained up to `keep_recent_blocks`; if necessary, fewer
older blocks are kept to fit the limit. Tool calls/results are never split.

Omitted history is compressed into a bounded, explicitly labeled **user-role
data** message. It is not elevated into a system instruction. The summary
takes the position of the newest omitted message: when older tool blocks of
the current turn are dropped, it follows the current question and precedes
the retained recent blocks, so the chronology stays intact. The built-in
`ExtractiveCompressor` preserves bounded excerpts of recent omitted entries,
including tool ids/results. It is lossy: it does not guarantee retention of
every fact or infer a semantic summary. Keep critical task state in explicit
application data or retrieve it from the full session archive.

rewrites the whole run state, so a long session eventually approaches the
store's byte limit (64 MiB by default for both `FileSessionStore` and
`FileRunStore`; keep the session limit at least as large as the run limit).
To avoid a run that completes but can no longer be saved or committed, work is
refused **before** it starts:

- `begin_turn` (and so `run_turn`) rejects a new turn with
  `RuntimeError::StorageLimit` once the serialized session exceeds half of the
  session store's limit. Nothing is bound or dispatched.
- The new input and the metadata needed to close its turn must also fit;
  oversized input is rejected before the active binding is written.
- Managed execution subtracts the complete session commit metadata from its
  byte allowance. A durable run reserves the largest declared model/tool
  response, duplicated tool state, context projection and a terminal-record
  margin before dispatch. Insufficient space produces `Storage
chunk.title: Sessions and bounded model context

chunk.text:
ut must never be treated as permission to start another job.

Only completed runs commit automatically. A failed terminal turn remains
bound until `abandon_turn` records an authenticated operator/application actor
and note. Uncertain/in-flight tools must first be reconciled through the
durable controller. Known observations stay in conversation history; calls
that were never dispatched receive explicit host error results. This includes
a call whose earlier attempt was reconciled with `RetrySafe` when the retry
itself never started; a call whose current attempt may have been dispatched
is never closed this way. An `Abort` reconciliation resolves the call with an
error result, after which the turn can be closed. A host note
records the failed outcome. This prevents an incomplete tool protocol from
leaking into the following model request, or a new question from silently
forgetting an uncertain write.

`commit_turn`/`abandon_turn` accept trusted controller state, not arbitrary
client-supplied JSON. The host application authenticates session access and
operator identity. A session is conversation state, not a cross-turn money
budget; each durable run keeps its own configured limits.

The supplied image's Python supervisor runs as **container PID 1 and uid 0**,
with only SETUID/SETGID capabilities. Its untrusted child runs as uid/gid 65534,
without those privileges, and cannot signal the root monitor. The monitor owns
the wall deadline and combined stdout/stderr byte ceiling. It returns a bounded
JSON packet and exits container PID 1 on timeout, excessive output or completion,
causing the container runtime to kill remaining namespace processes even if
they detached from the original process group. This deadline survives loss of
the host controller; it does not depend solely on killing `docker run`.
Ingress is also nonblocking and deadline-bound if the controller dies before
stdin EOF. Final response writing has a 500 ms grace before unconditional PID 1
exit, so an abandoned/nonreading output connection cannot keep code running.

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer
uses the same project control lock, including Application/API/CLI, workflows,
sessions, memory extraction and direct `db.runs(scope)` calls. Creating another
pool or omitting a quota from a process configuration does not bypass a stored
policy. File journals do not gain distributed quotas.

service charges remain separately unknown. A generation quota is not a durable
task queue, a rate limit or per-user billing. Separate

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer
uses the same project control lock, including Application/API/CLI, workflows,
sessions, memory extraction and direct `db.runs(scope)` calls. Creating another

cases.query: What happens when a memory snapshot is corrupt?

chunk.text:
OS locks, verify CAS/audit prefixes, flush a temporary file
and atomically replace the previous snapshot. Reads fail on corruption; they
do not silently reset state. Limits are 16 MiB, 4096 records, 16,384 forgotten
source bindings and 20,000 audit events. Admission also reserves 2 KiB, one
possible tombstone and one possible erasure event per retained record, so
administrative forgetting is not stranded by an admitted full snapshot.
A limit refuses the operation without
replacing the valid snapshot. Export/backup before planned migration; retain
the scope and revisions when implementing another `MemoryStore`.

Extraction request IDs bind a scope and the exact selected input to a durable
`memory-<hash>` child. Repeating a completed request with a fresh inspected
memory revision reuses its answer without another model request. If memory CAS
or capacity fails after generation, the completed extraction run stays in the
run store; inspect it and retry the **same request ID**, with the correct
revision/configuration. Do not silently mint a new paid request. Interrupting
generation preserves its spending uncertainty; normal interrupted-model
recovery can admit a further attempt within th

generation preserves its spending uncertainty; normal interrupted-model
recovery can admit a further attempt within the original cap. API admission
is released even if the extraction caller drops its future.

Forgetting physically removes every candidate/current/superseded/rejected
version of that slot from the memory snapshot. It retains only audit record
hashes and source-binding tombstones, preventing an old extraction of that same
source/slot from resurrecting the value, even if a later extractor proposes
different wording. A genuinely new user statement can propose the slot again.
This is memory-store erasure, not secure disk wiping or deletion of source
sessions, completed extraction runs, already frozen turn inputs, exports or
external backups. Those histories remain independently retained. New recalls
exclude forgotten records; old frozen inputs remain reproducible.

# Journal diagnostics and explicit OpenTelemetry export

`runtime::observability` projects **validated saved journals** into a correlated
trace. It performs no model, embedding or tool calls. There is no process-global
subscriber, automatic uploader, implicit `OTEL_*` environment discovery or
send-on-drop behavior. Network export requires the optional `telemetry` feature;
the application feature includes it, while default features remain empty.

## Trace and time semantics

`TraceSnapshot::run`, `workflow` and `session` build run or parent traces.
Workflow/node/durable-run and session/turn/durable-run relationships come from
persisted references and exact initial-input bindings. Closed session children
also match the recorded report fingerprint. Unreferenced, duplicate or mismatched
children fail; absent children are counted. Active durable children can be found
through their frozen node context before an outcome returns to the parent.
Reads of separate records are individually atomic, **not** a cross-record
transaction or a guarantee that a live parent and child were read simultaneously.

Stable SHA-256-derived IDs use a trusted host namespace and logical identities.

chunk.text:
# Knowledge retrieval and source citations

Requires the preview's `runtime` feature. The complete offline pipeline is:

```sh
cargo run --locked --features runtime --example agent_research
```

It imports two Markdown files, chunks and indexes them, exposes a permitted
read-only search tool to a durable agent, writes a cited report, and verifies
both exact quotations against the archived tool evidence. The example model
is deterministic and free. Replace it with the existing gateway model adapter
for provider execution; tool permissions and citation checks remain the same.

## Extension contracts

`runtime::rag` separates four host-controlled interfaces:

| Interface | Built-in implementation | Replacement contract |
|---|---|---|
| `DocumentLoader` | `TextLoader`: bounded UTF-8 text/Markdown file | Return a validated document with stable ID, source, title and extracted text; host decides external access |
| `Chunker` | `WindowChunker`: character windows with overlap | Preserve exact source text, UTF-8 byte offsets and provenance through `Chunk::from_range` |
| `CorpusStore` | `FileCorpusStore`: atomic versioned local snapshots | Consistent snapshots and atomic replacement/removal
chunk.title: Knowledge retrieval and source citations

chunk.text:
ing citations.

A quote must be an exact substring of the cited chunk and long enough to be
meaningful: by default at least 12 non-whitespace characters, or 3 words, or
6 CJK (Han/kana/Hangul) characters, whichever is met first. Use
`SearchResult::verify_with`/`verify_all_with` and `QuotePolicy` to change
these minimums; `verify`/`verify_all`, the app and benchmarks use the default.

What this proves, precisely: each cited chunk appeared in the supplied tool
output, its ID equals the hash of its own content, and the quote occurs in it.
The chunk ID is a *self*-hash. It detects accidental corruption, not tampering:
whoever can edit archived tool output can edit a chunk and recompute its ID,
and the edited chunk then verifies. It is not compared with the original
document's hash or the current corpus, and the app accepts output of any tool
step named `knowledge_search`. Integrity therefore rests on the durable run
store. Binding evidence to a specific tool instance/corpus (for example signed
or store-anchored results) is future work.

`VerifiedReport` retains exact chunks and corpus revision, so a saved report
can still be audited after the corpus is updated or deleted. The durable r

deleting documents is a separate explicit host action.

Retrieved text can contain malicious instructions. The supplied examples treat
it as untrusted evidence in the system prompt, and tool policy independently
controls capabilities. Prompt wording does not provide a security sandbox.
External retriever service charges are outside the agent's model-spend budget.

## Citation verification and its limits

Ask the model for `CitedReport { text, citations: [{ chunk_id, quote }] }`.
The text uses `[[full_chunk_id]]` references. Validate it using the actual
`SearchResult::verify` from the run's tool output, not a new search of a possibly
updated corpus. Verification rejects unknown/unretrieved sources, duplicate
citations, chunks whose text no longer matches their own ID, absent or invented
quotes, quotes below the minimum size, absent/unclosed markers and references
without corresponding citations.

still require a host loader. Sources are data; their references are not
automatically followed. This library does not sandbox custom loaders.

`ingest` validates document and plugin chunks before changing storage. Importing
the same document ID atomically replaces its prior chunks; it does not append

# Knowledge retrieval and source citations

Requires the preview's `runtime` feature. The complete offline pipeline is:

```sh
cargo run --locked --features runtime --example agent_research
```

It imports two Markdown files, chunks and indexes them, exposes a permitted
read-only search tool to a durable agent, writes a cited report, and verifies
both exact quotations against the archived tool evidence. The example model
is deterministic and free. Replace it with the existing gateway model adapter
for provider execution; tool permissions and citation checks remain the same.

| Interface | Built-in implementation | Replacement contract |
|---|---|---|
| `DocumentLoader` | `TextLoader`: bounded UTF-8 text/Markdown file | Return a validated document with stable ID, source, title and extracted text; host decides external access |

| `CorpusStore` | `FileCorpusStore`: atomic versioned local snapshots | Consistent snapshots and atomic replacement/removal

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer
uses the same project control lock, including Application/API/CLI, workflows,

policy. File journals do not gain distributed quotas.

service charges remain separately unknown. A generation quota is not a durable
task queue, a rate limit or per-user billing. Separate

chunk.text:
# Explicit Linux-container Python execution

The optional `sandbox` feature exposes `CodeSandbox`, `DockerSandbox` and
`SandboxTool`. `app` includes the feature but registers no execution tool until
the host supplies `sandbox` configuration. Even then, only workflow roles that
list the tool receive it, unless `sandbox_top_level` is set. A missing Docker engine, missing
image or failed container never falls back to host Python or a host shell.

## Isolation contract

Only code is model-controlled. The host fixes the Docker CLI, local engine
socket/pipe, immutable audited image, platform, CPU/memory/output/time limits.
The model cannot select an executable, image, mount, network, package, device,
environment variable or Docker option. Code is sent through stdin, not shell

journaling. The built-in `GatewayTransport` follows this contract for retries

The `app,database` features provide explicit SQLite/PostgreSQL project queues
and independent worker processes. Submission persists immutable task input and

## Session size limit

Every turn's run starts from the full session history, and each checkpoint
rewrites the whole run state, so a long session eventually approaches the
store's byte limit (64 MiB by default for both `FileSessionStore` and
`FileRunStore`; keep the session limit at least as large as the run limit).
To avoid a run that completes but can no longer be saved or committed, work is
refused **before** it starts:

- `begin_turn` (and so `run_turn`) rejects a new turn with
  `RuntimeError::StorageLimit` once the serialized session exceeds half of the
  session store's limit. Nothing is bound or dispatched.
- The new input and the metadata needed to close its turn must also fit;
  oversized input is rejected before the active binding is written.
- Managed execution subtracts the complete session commit metadata from its
  byte allowance. A durable run reserves the largest declared model/tool

1. Planner produces a bounded list of tasks.
2. Executors consume distinct task selectors concurrently, exactly once per
   completed child. Extra worker slots skip.
3. Writer consumes the plan and executor outputs.
4. Reviewer returns `{ "approved": bool, "feedback": string }`.
5. A rejected draft is rewritten with previous draft/feedback, within
   `max_revisions`; executor effects are retained. Approval skips later rounds.
6. `result` selects the first approved draft. Exhausted revisions fail rather
   than treating an unapproved draft as success.

Planner/writer/reviewer must be pure transforms or native durable agent roles
with only read-only tools. Put side effects in executors. This prevents a
review rewrite from implicitly repeating a publishing/write role. Tool
implementations still must tell the truth about effects. PEER provides basic
bounded coordination; distributed workers, arbitrary cyclic graphs, dynamic
team formation and semantic report quality evaluation are not implemented.

## Recovery and effects

The workflow saves an intent and spending allocation before polling a handler.
Completed nodes are never invoked again. Each handler declares one contract:

| Recovery | Implementer obligation | After process interruption |
|---|---|---|
| `Pure` | No effects, paid I/O or usage; zero cost ceiling | Safe recomputation |
| `DurableChild` | Reenter the exact stable child ID/input; child owns effects and spending journal | Reenter child and observe its state |
| `Manual` | Any other effectful implementation | Mark uncertain; operator must record observed output or abort |

The event log is not capped: load-time validation checks every node's
dispatch counter against its `NodeStarted` events, so dropping old events

## Session size limit

Every turn's run starts from the full session history, and each checkpoint
rewrites the whole run state, so a long session eventually approaches the
store's byte limit (64 MiB by default for both `FileSessionStore` and
`FileRunStore`; keep the session limit at least as large as the run limit).

refused **before** it starts:

- `begin_turn` (and so `run_turn`) rejects a new turn with
  `RuntimeError::StorageLimit` once the serialized session exceeds half of the
  session store's limit. Nothing is bound or dispatched.
- The new input and the metadata needed to close its turn must also fit;
  oversized input is rejected before the active binding is written.

  byte allowance. A durable run reserves the largest declared model/tool
  response, duplicated tool state, context projection and a terminal-record
  margin before dispatch. Insufficient space produces `Storage

# Project generation quotas

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer
uses the same project control lock, including Application/API/CLI, workflows,
sessions, memory extraction and direct `db.runs(scope)` calls. Creating another
pool or omitting a quota from a process configuration does not bypass a stored
policy. File journals do not gain distributed quotas.

service charges remain separately unknown. A generation quota is not a durable
task queue, a rate limit or per-user billing. Separate

The supplied image's Python supervisor runs as **container PID 1 and uid 0**,
with only SETUID/SETGID capabilities. Its untrusted child runs as uid/gid 65534,
without those privileges, and cannot signal the root monitor. The monitor owns
the wall deadline and combined stdout/stderr byte ceiling. It returns a bounded

causing the container runtime to kill remaining namespace processes even if
they detached from the original process group. This deadline survives loss of
the host controller; it does not depend solely on killing `docker run`.
Ingress is also nonblocking and deadline-bound if the controller dies before
stdin EOF. Final response writing has a 500 ms grace before unconditional PID 1
exit, so an abandoned/nonreading output connection cannot keep code running.

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer

# Project generation quotas

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer
uses the same project control lock, including Application/API/CLI, workflows,
sessions, memory extraction and direct `db.runs(scope)` calls. Creating another
pool or omitting a quota from a process configuration does not bypass a stored
policy. File journals do not gain distributed quotas.

This is generation accounting. Embedding has its separate ledger; generic tool
service charges remain separately unknown. A generation quota is not a durable
task queue, a rate limit or per-user billing. Separate
[queue/worker and bounded load evidence](durable-queue.md) covers those service
operations; broad native quality remains in P0.

db.migrate().await?;

let current = quota.sn

## Accounting and recovery

Admission and the run's reservation journal commit in the same transaction,
before provider dispatch. The lock order is runtime ownership, project quota,
then accounting records. Administrator imports lock the project control row
and read committed journals without taking runtime leases. PostgreSQL row locks
and SQLite's immediate writer serialize competing processes.

Held cost is `committed_micros + in_flight_micros`. Uncertain cost is already
included in committed and is not counted twice. Outstanding attempts are
`in_flight_attempts + uncertain_attempts`: zero-priced requests occupy slots.
Known settlement releases only that attempt's slot. A lost response or killed
process retains its ceiling and slot; converting in-flight into uncertain does
not free capacity. The ledger does not silently refund or erase uncertain work.

A quota `Budget` refusal means a transaction was rolled back and no dispatch
was admitted. The runtime removes only the refused reservation and records the
budget stop without inventing uncertain fees. Other storage/commit failures
remain ambiguous and retain conservative uncertainty. Reservation registration
is seriali

## Schema-v2 migration

Schema v2 introduced the generation-quota barrier. The current
`SqlDatabase::migrate` / `taskloom database-migrate` creates schema v3 or upgrades
v1/v2 in one transaction, including queue indexes/ownership. Stop all old hosts and workers first. Upgrade
refuses while any database-clock lease is live; PostgreSQL also locks the lease
table during the version barrier. Dataset UUID and existing version-1 JSON
envelopes/runtime checkpoints are preserved. Unknown versions and downgrades are
refused. Back up the complete database before upgrading and restore the complete
backup with its matching binary if rollback is required.

# Data-only skills, templates and connectors

The `runtime` SDK and optional `app` host support installable, content-pinned
skill packages. They contain UTF-8 guidance, typed role/output contracts,
workflow templates and connector configuration examples. Installation stores
inert JSON objects: it does not execute scripts, register a tool, start a

description, SHA-256 for every asset, exact dependency `{name,version,digest}`
pins, tool effects/permissions, required credential **names**, roles, templates
and optional connector-example metadata. Names use lowercase ASCII letters,

triples. Ranges, prereleases, network URLs, i

`ingest` validates document and plugin chunks before changing storage. Importing
the same document ID atomically replaces its prior chunks; it does not append

mutating the existing corpus.

File storage captures an absolute root, serializes writers with an OS lock,
validates existing snapshots, and atomically replaces `corpus.json`. The default

chunk.text:
# Knowledge retrieval and source citations

Requires the preview's `runtime` feature. The complete offline pipeline is:

```sh
cargo run --locked --features runtime --example agent_research
```

It imports two Markdown files, chunks and indexes them, exposes a permitted
read-only search tool to a durable agent, writes a cited report, and verifies
both exact quotations against the archived tool evidence. The example model
is deterministic and free. Replace it with the existing gateway model adapter
for provider execution; tool permissions and citation checks remain the same.

## Extension contracts

`runtime::rag` separates four host-controlled interfaces:

| Interface | Built-in implementation | Replacement contract |
|---|---|---|
| `DocumentLoader` | `TextLoader`: bounded UTF-8 text/Markdown file | Return a validated document with stable ID, source, title and extracted text; host decides external access |
| `Chunker` | `WindowChunker`: character windows with overlap | Preserve exact source text, UTF-8 byte offsets and provenance through `Chunk::from_range` |
| `CorpusStore` | `FileCorpusStore`: atomic versioned local snapshots | Consistent snapshots and atomic replacement/removal
chunk.title: Knowledge retrieval and source citations

chunk.text:
ing citations.

A quote must be an exact substring of the cited chunk and long enough to be
meaningful: by default at least 12 non-whitespace characters, or 3 words, or
6 CJK (Han/kana/Hangul) characters, whichever is met first. Use
`SearchResult::verify_with`/`verify_all_with` and `QuotePolicy` to change
these minimums; `verify`/`verify_all`, the app and benchmarks use the default.

What this proves, precisely: each cited chunk appeared in the supplied tool
output, its ID equals the hash of its own content, and the quote occurs in it.
The chunk ID is a *self*-hash. It detects accidental corruption, not tampering:
whoever can edit archived tool output can edit a chunk and recompute its ID,
and the edited chunk then verifies. It is not compared with the original
document's hash or the current corpus, and the app accepts output of any tool
step named `knowledge_search`. Integrity therefore rests on the durable run

# Knowledge retrieval and source citations

Requires the preview's `runtime` feature. The complete offline pipeline is:

```sh
cargo run --locked --features runtime --example agent_research
```

It imports two Markdown files, chunks and indexes them, exposes a permitted
read-only search tool to a durable agent, writes a cited report, and verifies
both exact quotations against the archived tool evidence. The example model
is deterministic and free. Replace it with the existing gateway model adapter
for provider execution; tool permissions and citation checks remain the same.

| Interface | Built-in implementation | Replacement contract |

| `Chunker` | `WindowChunker`: character windows with overlap | Preserve exact source text, UTF-8 byte offsets and provenance through `Chunk::from_range` |
| `CorpusStore` | `FileCorpusStore`: atomic versioned local snapshots | Consistent snapshots and atomic replacement/removal

`research` adds bounded webpage/search clients and an explicitly configured
Poppler PDF loader. `app` includes this feature but grants no web or PDF access
by default. Vector/hybrid retrieval is available with `runtime` alone.
These additions do not change the existing `AgentTask` API.

# Project generation quotas

The opt-in SQL stores enforce one cumulative monetary cap and one outstanding
attempt cap per authenticated host-selected tenant/project. Every SQL run writer
uses the same project control lock, including Application/API/CLI, workflows,
sessions, memory extraction and direct `db.runs(scope)` calls. Creating another
pool or omitting a quota from a process configuration does not bypass a stored
policy. File journals do not gain distributed quotas.

This is generation accounting. Embedding has its separate ledger; generic tool
service charges remain separately unknown. A generation quota is not a durable
task queue, a rate limit or per-user billing. Separate
[queue/worker and bounded load evidence](durable-queue.md) covers those service
operations; broad native quality remains in P0.

## Accounting and recovery

Admission and the run's reservation journal commit in the same transaction,
before provider dispatch. The lock order is runtime ownership, project quota,
then accounting records. Administrator imports lock the project control row
and read committed journals without taking runtime leases. PostgreSQL row locks
and SQLite's immediate writer serialize competing processes.

Held cost is `committed_micros + in_flight_micros`. Uncertain cost is already
included in committed and is not counted twice. Outstanding attempts are
`in_flight_attempts + uncertain_attempts`: zero-priced requests occupy slots.
Known settlement releases only that attempt's slot. A lost response or killed
process retains its ceiling and slot; converting in-flight into uncertain does
not free capacity. The ledger does not silently refund or erase uncertain work.

A quota `Budget` refusal means a transaction was rolled back and no dispatch
was admitted. The runtime removes only the refused reservation and records the

# Explicit Linux-container Python execution

The optional `sandbox` feature exposes `CodeSandbox`, `DockerSandbox` and
`SandboxTool`. `app` includes the feature but registers no execution tool until
the host supplies `sandbox` configuration. Even then, only workflow roles that
list the tool receive it, unless `sandbox_top_level` is set. A missing Docker engine, missing
image or failed container never falls back to host Python or a host shell.

## Isolation contract

Only code is model-controlled. The host fixes the Docker CLI, local engine
socket/pipe, immutable audited image, platform, CPU/memory/output/time limits.
The model cannot select an executable, image, mount, network, package, device,
environment variable or Docker option. Code is sent through stdin, not shell
command text or host argv interpolation. The host passes only the code's byte
length and SHA-256 as supervisor arguments (`--code-bytes`, `--code-sha256`).
End of stdin alone does not prove the write completed, because an interrupted
controller also closes stdin. The supervisor therefore refuses to run anything
unless it received exactly the declared bytes with the declared digest. On
refusal it returns exit code 12

without those privileges, and cannot signal the root monitor. The monitor owns

exit, so an abandoned/nonreading output connection cannot keep code running.

# Durable SQL queues and workers

The `app,database` features provide explicit SQLite/PostgreSQL project queues
and independent worker processes. Submission persists immutable task input and
host contracts before execution. Workers reuse the existing durable run,
workflow, PEER and session controllers; a second job log never decides that an

submission/control currently uses the queue API or CLI. Legacy `job.active`
fields describe process-local workers. **Use queue job state and its runtime
bindings for distributed activity**, including a worker running on another host.
